title: Hedging US Growth Stocks
gist: Gavekal teaser: US growth stocks have stayed resilient despite higher oil prices and bond yields this year, lagging value by only 3.7pp versus a repeat of 2022; the piece asks what could derail them and how to hedge, but the hedging content is paywalled.

insights.claim: The MSCI US growth index has outperformed its value counterpart generally since 2007, with only a brief reversal during the 2022 surge in bond yields before growth regained the upper hand in 2023.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Growth leadership has survived rate shocks; the 2022 episode is the template for a reversal.
insights.locator: US growth stocks have proved remarkably resilient

insights.claim: Despite this year's jump in oil prices and US bond yields, the MSCI US growth index has lagged value by only 3.7pp year to date, rather than repeating the 2022 sell-off in growth.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Growth is absorbing an oil and yield shock better than in 2022; complacency risk if shocks intensify.
insights.quote: The MSCI US growth index has lagged the value index by just 3.7pp so far this year.
insights.locator: US growth stocks have proved remarkably resilient

insights.claim: Gavekal's framing is that when everything is going well prudent investors should look for pitfalls, and it asks what could derail US growth stock strength and how to hedge those risks; the specific answers are behind the paywall.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Consider hedges for a growth-stock pullback, but the article provides no actionable specifics in the teaser.
insights.locator: But when everything is going well
